title: Streamline assistive guidance and inline actions for multimode input fields
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: We have inconsistent placement and behavior of inline actions (clear, password-reveal, prefix/suffix controls) and assistive guidance (helper text, validation messages) across density modes and breakpoints. This causes cramped mobile layouts, overlapping microcopy, and unpredictable screen reader announcements. Goal: define a single, layout-aware pattern for multimode input fields that harmonizes token usage, hit targets, and ARIA verbosity so that inputs behave predictably across compact/regular/comfortable density and on mobile devices.
acceptance_criteria: Define token mappings for padding, icon spacing, and helper-row height for all density modes
Provide a deterministic ordering and animation guideline for inline actions (left/right) so they never overlap helper text at small widths
Document ARIA roles/attributes and screen-reader phrasing for error vs soft-help states
Ship three composable CSS utility classes that implement the layout-aware input scaffolding: .ri-input--compact, .ri-input--wrap-actions, .ri-input--assistive-inline
Unit and visual regression tests for Chrome/Safari on desktop and iOS/Android mobile widths
Design handoff artifacts (Figma) and a reviewed GitHub PR with implementation guidance in README
decisions: Use a two-line assistive area (primary helper / secondary validation) with truncation rules instead of collapsing into a single line on small screens
Inline actions will always have a minimum 40x40 hit target; when space is constrained they move into an overflow menu icon on the right
Prefer polite ARIA live region for helper text and assertive for error messages; include a visually hidden prefix for errors to improve NVDA/VoiceOver clarity
Do not introduce new tokens; map to existing spacing and typography tokens with an alias layer to simplify future token swaps
engineering_notes: ENG-4120 will add layout utilities and the overflow menu component; coordinate to avoid duplicate CSS variables
Implementation should reuse existing icon components and avoid creating per-input images to keep bundle size stable
Consider adding a small heuristic in the runtime that toggles .ri-input--wrap-actions at < 320px to force overflow behavior for embedded webviews
Performance: avoid layout flushes by computing action overflow in CSS where possible (flex + min-width) and falling back to JS only for older browsers
